welcome.title: Welcome to Jarvis
welcome.lead: A few steps and your Jarvis is ready. Everything stays on your device at home; only the AI provider you pick next receives selected text to analyse.

account.title: Your access
account.lead: You find the setup code in the admin service log. Then choose a password for the admin area.

database.title: Existing data
database.lead: This device already holds a Jarvis archive. Enter its two passwords, otherwise Jarvis cannot reach your messages. They are in your old .env or your password manager.

name.title: What's your name?
name.lead: Jarvis uses it in summaries and profiles.

provider.title: AI provider
provider.lead: Jarvis needs a language model to sort chats, suggest replies and answer your questions. Any provider with an OpenAI-compatible API works, including a model running at home.

models.title: Models
models.lead: One model per job. Small models are fine for sorting; replies and questions benefit from a stronger one.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.lead: Decide what must never reach the AI. This applies from the first message.

features.title: What Jarvis may do
features.lead: You can change all of this later in settings.

remote.title: On the go
remote.lead: Optional. A Cloudflare tunnel lets you reach Jarvis and the app outside your Wi-Fi without opening ports. You enter the public address in the app later.

review.title: Check everything
review.lead: This gets saved, then Jarvis starts its services.

consent.lead: Two things you should know and confirm.

consent.whatsapp: Jarvis is an independent project and not affiliated with WhatsApp or Meta. The WhatsApp connection is unofficial (Baileys as a linked device), may violate the WhatsApp Terms of Service and can get my account banned.

consent.responsibility: Your archive contains other people's messages; you are responsible for handling them lawfully (e.g. GDPR).
consent.providerNote: Message content, including your contacts', is sent to {{provider}} for analysis.

legal.title: Legal notes
legal.sub: Short and honest, what you should know.

sections.title: Independent project
sections.body: Jarvis is an independent open-source project. It is not affiliated with, supported or approved by WhatsApp or Meta. WhatsApp is a trademark of WhatsApp LLC.

sections.title: Unofficial WhatsApp connection
sections.body: Jarvis connects to your WhatsApp account as a linked device through the Baileys library. This is not an official interface and may violate the WhatsApp Terms of Service. WhatsApp can restrict or ban your account, and the connection can stop working at any time. Use it at your own risk; consider a secondary number.

sections.title: AI provider
sections.body: If you enable AI features, message content is sent to the configured AI provider (for example OpenAI), including messages from your contacts, voice transcripts and image descriptions. The provider's terms and privacy policy apply. Excluded chats and redaction limit this. Without a key, processing stays local.

sections.title: Other people's messages
sections.body: The archive contains messages from other people. You are responsible for handling them lawfully, for example under the GDPR.

sections.title: No warranty
sections.body: Jarvis is provided as is, without warranty of any kind.

name.title: What should your assistant be called?
name.lead: Your private context manager runs on your own hardware. You set it up once and use it in the browser or the mobile app.

account.title: Your access to {{name}}
account.done: Your password is set. It works for web, mobile and administration.
account.lead: Whoever sets a password here first becomes the owner of this installation. Choose your own password for web, mobile and administration.
account.passwordHelp: 15 to 200 characters. A long passphrase is easy to remember. Password managers are supported.

source.title: What do you want to connect?
source.lead: Right now you can connect WhatsApp. More sources can be added later.
source.warn: Jarvis uses an unofficial WhatsApp connection. WhatsApp does not officially support this; your account could be restricted or banned.
source.archive: Messages and metadata are archived on your server. You set up the AI provider in a moment. WhatsApp decides how much history is imported.
source.consent: I have read the notes and want to connect WhatsApp

wa.title: Link WhatsApp
wa.later: You can link WhatsApp later under Connections.
wa.how: Open WhatsApp on your phone → Settings or menu → Linked devices → Link a device. Then scan this QR code.
wa.expired: The code expired. A new one appears automatically.
wa.phone: Or: phone number with country code
wa.codeHelp: On your phone choose “Link with phone number instead” and enter this code.

ai.title: Connect {{name}}'s AI
ai.lead: {{name}} is an AI assistant: it understands your messages, sorts them into topics, describes images and answers your questions. For that it needs an AI provider. OpenRouter is the easiest: sign in, done.
ai.cost: Texts, audio and images are sent to the provider and API costs apply. Chat exclusions apply to search and topic sorting, not automatically to audio and images. Decide below what must never reach the AI.
ai.more: Other settings such as transcription, image descriptions and topic sorting start with sensible values and can be changed later under Settings.
ai.orLead: Sign in to OpenRouter or create an account there. You come back here automatically and {{name}} takes the key by itself. Add some credit at OpenRouter, 5 $ is enough to start.
ai.orLimits: With OpenRouter voice messages stay without text and search runs on your device. Both work with an OpenAI key.
ai.orNoRedirect: Not coming back? Paste the code by hand
ai.orCodeHelp: OpenRouter shows a code after you sign in. Copy it here.

remote.title: Where do you want to use {{name}}?
remote.lead: To begin with we recommend your home network. You can set up access on the go any time later.
remote.localLead: Your devices reach the server in the same home network. On the go you will need remote access or a VPN later. HTTP in the home network is not encrypted.
remote.localHelp: Leave empty: Jarvis finds the home network address itself. If your server is in several networks, enter the right address here.
remote.warn: After sign-in, settings and maintenance are also reachable at this address. Your password protects the whole installation. With a tunnel, Cloudflare relays the traffic.
remote.cf1: 1. Sign in to Cloudflare and use a domain managed there.
remote.cf2: 2. Create a Cloudflared tunnel. Copy its token here; you do not need to run Cloudflare's install command.
remote.cf3: 3. Add a published application route. As service choose HTTP and enter app-web:8084. That address only exists inside Docker.
remote.ownLead: Forward your HTTPS address to Jarvis' web entry (local port 8081). Use the same address for web and mobile.
remote.check: When you continue, Jarvis starts remote access and checks that the address really points to this server.
remote.localOnly: Use only the home network for now

done.title: {{name}} is ready.
done.lead: In the browser you sign in with your password right away. In the mobile app you first scan this code or enter the server address, then sign in.
done.localOnly: This address only works on the server itself. Add a home network address under System → Settings → Access & remote access before you connect the mobile app.
done.qr: The QR code only contains the server address, no password and no sign-in token.
done.mcpTitle: Connect Claude and other AI clients
done.mcp: {{name}} comes with an MCP server. With it your AI client can search your archive, fetch context and run the actions you allow. Connect it at this address and sign in with your password.
done.mcpRemote: Cloud clients such as Claude need an HTTPS address reachable from outside. You can set up remote access later.
done.mcpLater: You find this connection again under System → Connections.
done.reading: Jarvis is now reading in your history. The home screen shows how far import, transcription, search and sorting are. The first cards appear bit by bit.

task.offline: Your server cannot be reached right now. Setup may keep running there. As soon as the connection is back, this continues.

explain.install: Jarvis downloads its building blocks and starts them. How long this takes depends on your internet connection.
explain.start: Everything is starting up. We wait until each part is ready.
explain.finish: Checking that your archive is reachable. Almost there.

status.summary: {{messages}} messages in {{chats}} chats · {{named}} of {{contacts}} contacts with names

waiting.organizer: Waiting for conversations to settle, or for the daily budget.
waiting.search: The search model is still loading.
waiting.people: Starts when sorting takes a break.

status.searchReady: Meaning search is ready: ask Jarvis something, it also finds messages that use other words.
status.searchNotReady: Meaning search is still starting. Word search already works.
status.note: This keeps running in the background, even if you close the page. New cards show up bit by bit.
status.namesMissing_one: One contact has no name yet. Names come from your phone's address book and from profile names in new messages.
status.namesMissing_other: {{count}} contacts have no name yet. Names come from your phone's address book and from profile names in new messages.
status.namesGained_one: One more contact has a name now.
status.namesGained_other: {{count}} more contacts have a name now.
status.namesSame: No new names. People who are not in your address book get their name with their next message.

learning.title: Learning
learning.areaSub: What Jarvis learned from "Later", "Not important" and "Important"
learning.sub: Your choices shape what comes first. Everything here can be changed or undone.
learning.removed: Rule removed. The cards show up as before.
learning.how: If you mark something in a chat as not important or later three times and never as important, Jarvis shows new cards from that chat as "Later". Marking a chat important twice makes it important. Five times not important for the same kind of card applies to that kind. Nothing is deleted: rules only change the order and what is shown.
learning.toggleHelp: Off: Jarvis creates no new rules. Existing ones stay until you remove them.
learning.empty: No rules yet. They appear when you mark cards as later, not important or important.
learning.addChatHint: For a whole chat: tap a card and choose "Everything from …" at the bottom.
learning.forgetConfirm: Delete all learned rules and counters? Rules you set yourself stay.

health.allGoodSub: Jarvis receives messages and every part works.

serviceDown.title: {{service}} is not running
serviceDown.detail: This part of Jarvis has stopped. A restart usually fixes it.

serviceUnhealthy.title: {{service}} has problems
serviceUnhealthy.detail: This part runs but does not answer properly. Try a restart.

waLoggedOut.title: WhatsApp was logged out
waLoggedOut.detail: Jarvis is no longer a linked device on your phone. No new messages arrive until you link again.

waNotLinked.title: WhatsApp is not linked yet
waNotLinked.detail: Scan the code with WhatsApp on your phone so Jarvis receives messages.

waDisconnected.title: WhatsApp is not connected right now
waDisconnected.detail: Jarvis keeps trying by itself. If your phone was offline, Jarvis catches up afterwards. If this stays, link again.

diskFull.title: Storage is almost full
diskFull.detail: Soon Jarvis cannot store messages any more. Use a larger SD card or delete other files on the device.

diskLow.title: Storage is getting low
diskLow.detail: Everything still runs, but plan for a larger SD card.

updateFailed.title: The last update did not work
updateFailed.detail: Jarvis keeps running the previous version. It tries again next night.
